items.PAYLOAD: Theory of Adaptive Epistemic Systems is a theoretical framework for intelligence as reality-coupled causal self-correction.
Intelligence is proposed to require empirical modification of future-generating mechanisms, and authority restoration is proposed to require demonstrated viability rather than internal consistency.
Defines adaptive authority dynamics, mechanisms/authority, and residuals as the core conceptual vocabulary.
Defines Reality->Residual->Attribution->Authority Update->Mechanism Change->Future Behavior, exponential attenuation, and dOmega/dt<=Theta C.
Predicts improved adaptation from authority-level modification under shifts, contradiction, delayed feedback, changing constraints, and adversarial conditions.
Asserts RAHU as the experimental instrument for testing adaptive authority dynamics; no endpoint identity or edge is inferred.
Repository is described as the theoretical foundation; the framework explicitly remains an empirical hypothesis intended for refinement.
Causal-authority identification, beta/law validation, Omega/Theta/C measurement, and RAHU endpoint/validation standing remain unresolved.
Paper proposes Adaptive Epistemic Systems and Adaptive Authority Dynamics as a formal basis for persistent long-horizon adaptation.

Central theory claims distinguish mechanism-level adaptation from output recovery, define authority as causal influence, state qualitative consequences of attenuation, motivate representation expansion, and conclude that experience must reshape future-generating mechanisms.
Defines Adaptive Epistemic System and mechanism/authority concepts.
Formalizes mechanism-level updating, residual attribution Phi_R(e_t,m_i), mechanism-specific exponential attenuation, and the stability inequality.
Restoration is proposed to require measurable gains in grounded reachability and correction capacity.
Authored comparisons to neighboring learning paradigms and assertion that RAHU is designed to test the theory.
Predicts lower recurrence, better shift adaptation, faster recovery, improved viability, and reduced future probability of repeated error classes.
Mechanism decomposition, Phi_R identification, restoration measurement, expansion threshold, and empirical comparison remain unresolved; no results are reported.
Citation metadata records title, author, version 0.1.0, release date, repository, type 'software', and research keywords.
Citation abstract restates persistent mechanism modification and Adaptive Authority Dynamics according to demonstrated viability.
Citation type 'software' does not establish executable implementation on the frozen surface.
Contribution policy invites challenge, refinement, and falsification of the framework.
Specifies theoretical critique, formal-change justification, and desired experimental validation contribution types.
Experiments should distinguish authority-level adaptation from output/memory/policy/parameter changes, and theory-development influence should track explanatory performance.
Process rules prioritize evidence, definition preservation, falsifiability, explicit change rationale, modular/tested future code, reproducibility, and contributor attribution.
Prospective validation/code rules are not completed experiments or implementations, and governance analogy does not validate causal authority scientifically.
